heroText: Bodø works best as a base in Norway when you anchor days around Saltstraumen, Norwegian Aviation Museum and Bodo harbour. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Bodø International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: Origins
history.text: The municipality is named after the old Bodøgård farm (Old Norse: Boðvin), since the town was built on its ground.
The current version which is a simplified, modern version of the old arms was granted on 24 July 1959.

history.label: Growth
history.text: The first element might be boði which means "sunken rock" or "skerry" and the last element is vin which means "meadow" or "pasture".

history.label: Modern city
history.text: It showed a midnight sun above a boat on the sea in front of a mountain range.

history.label: Civic role
history.text: The official blazon is "Gules, a sun Or" (Norwegian: På rød bunn en gull sol).

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The sun was chosen since Bodø was the first town in Northern Norway, and it experiences the midnight sun every year.
